headline: High-risk shared-workspace and output-trust pathways exist: Perplexity can feed unverified web-derived content into transformers, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Perplexity can browse live web content and produce citations, while transformers can read files and process text/scripts. If Perplexity outputs are copied into transformers or a shared workspace, attacker-controlled content can be treated as instructions. This is not provably blocked by either profile, but the bridge is not automatic.
conditions: IF Perplexity output is pasted into transformers prompts or files
IF transformers parses copied content as instructions without a provenance filter
mitigations: Use a strict delimiter/template for copied content
Add a provenance note before any pasted Perplexity text
Disable instruction-following on imported text
Review one sample prompt for injection markers
requires-engineering: add content provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity touches uploaded documents and browsing context, and transformers can read/write files and use broad network egress. If they share a workspace or files are moved from Perplexity into transformers, sensitive document contents can flow into a broader-egress environment. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so the leakage path is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF uploaded PDFs or images from Perplexity are saved into a directory transformers can read
IF transformers sends those files or derived text to external services
mitigations: Keep Perplexity exports in a separate folder
Do not place sensitive files in the transformers workspace
Check one run for outbound requests
Redact sensitive fields before transfer
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Perplexity is vendor-hosted and does not write the host filesystem, but transformers has unrestricted local write, shell, and subprocess capability. If both are pointed at the same mutable directory or git checkout, transformers can overwrite artifacts that Perplexity later reads or summarizes. Because the profiles do not show locking or isolation, the conflict can corrupt shared work and is dangerous by default when co-located.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same local directory or git checkout
IF transformers writes files that Perplexity later ingests or summarizes
mitigations: Use separate working directories
Avoid shared git branches during parallel runs
Snapshot files before transformer writes
Check for concurrent edits before merging
requires-engineering: add file locks or orchestration-level coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity is an answer engine that emits cited summaries, and transformers can consume text and act as a document-processing pipeline. If transformers treats Perplexity output as authoritative, any hallucination or citation error can cascade into downstream documents or scripts. The pair lacks a documented verification step, so the unsafe default is to trust the upstream output too much.
conditions: IF transformers uses Perplexity output as source text without independent verification
IF downstream artifacts are generated from that output
mitigations: Require a second-source check for factual claims
Mark Perplexity text as untrusted input
Spot-check citations before reuse
Keep generated artifacts in draft status
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Perplexity is a closed-source vendor-hosted service that touches uploaded documents and browsing context, while transformers is open-source and locally runnable. The profiles do not specify a concrete residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance concern is visible: sensitive data may leave a local environment when sent to Perplexity. The other agent is not separately implicated by a documented policy gap.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded to Perplexity
IF local policy forbids vendor-hosted processing
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to Perplexity
Use synthetic or redacted samples
Confirm retention settings before upload
Document approved data classes
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing for regulated content
